Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 13 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Overview of PM Narendra Modi Visit to Gujarat from October 30 to 31, 2026 Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi visited Gujarat from 30 to 31 October 2026, during which he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for several infrastructure, agriculture, dairy and social welfare projects worth over Rs 14,400 crore across Banaskantha and Ekta Nagar in Narmada district, Gujarat. • He also participated in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) celebrations at Ekta Nagar on 31 October 2026, commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Overview of PM Modi visit to Gujarat ✓ Dates of Visit: October 30 to October 31, 2026 ✓ Total Cost of Projects: More than 14,400 crore, including Rs 14,000 crore in Banaskantha and Rs 400 crore in Ekta Nagar ✓ Visit to Banaskantha: ✓ Projects Inaugurated: BBBRC facility (Rs Rs 325 crore); ASRS Facility (Rs 31.14 crore); The French fries processing plant (Rs 51.65 crore) ✓ Other Key Highlight: Release of the 24th instalment of PM-KISAN (over Rs 18,690 crore), benefitting 9.34 crore eligible farmers ✓ Visit to Ekta Nagar: ✓ Key Highlight: Inauguration and laying of foundation stone of development projects ✓ Total Cost: Rs 426.71 crore ✓ Total Development Projects: 31, 23 development projects (worth Rs 307.83 crore); and 8 development projects (worth Rs 118.88 crore) Visit to Banaskantha: Inauguration of BBBRC: PM Modi inaugurated the Rs 325 crore Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre (BBRC) and its Embryo Transfer Technology–In Vitro Fertilisation (ET-IVF) laboratory at Bhildi, developed by Banas Dairy with technical support from the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB). Spread across 127 acres, it targets 25,000 high-quality embryos annually to improve indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds. Other Key Banas Dairy Projects: He inaugurated the Rs 31.14 crore Automated Storage and Retrieval System (ASRS) at Palanpur, with a capacity of 11,000 pallets, and the Rs 51.65 crore French fries processing plant at Sanadar, designed to increase production from 2 to 5 tonnes per hour. Bio-CNG Plants: He laid the foundation stones for two Bio- Compressed Natural Gas (Bio-CNG) plants at Tharad and Radhanpur, with cattle dung processing capacities of 75 and 100 Metric Tonnes (MT) per day, respectively. Metro and Road Projects: He laid the foundation stones for Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A (over 6 kilometres (km), 5 stations) and Phase-2B (3.3 km, 3 stations) and announced the Rs 2,600 crore widening of Ahmedabad– Mehsana State Highway (SH-41) from four to eight lanes. Railway Connectivity: He flagged off the Ahmedabad (Sabarmati)–Varanasi Express and Mehsana– Becharaji–Sabarmati Mainline Electric Multiple Unit (MEMU) train services. Anganwadi Centres: He laid the foundation stone for 4,030 child-friendly Anganwadi Centres and inaugurated 361 completed centres, involving an investment of Rs 800 crore.

About Gujarat: Chief Minister (CM)- Bhupendrabhai Patel Governor- Acharya Devvrat Capital- Gandhinagar National Parks (NP)- Gir NP, Marine NP PM Narendra Modi Approves Delhi–Guwahati Bullet Train Corridor via Siliguri On 31 October 2026, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved the 1,500 kilometers (km) Northern Bullet Train Corridor, connecting Delhi with Guwahati (Assam) via Siliguri (West Bengal, WB), enhancing regional connectivity, reducing travel time and boosting economic growth across northern, eastern and northeastern India. • The approval was announced by Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, Ministry of Railways (MoR), in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh (UP), during the flag-off ceremony of the Varanasi–New Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper Express. About Ministry of Railways(MoR): Union Minister- Ashwini Vaishnaw (Rajya Sabha- Odisha) Minister of State (MoS)- Veeranna Somanna (Constituency- Tumkur, Karnataka) India Hosts First-Ever BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise in Andaman and Nicobar Islands In October 2026, India’s Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC), an integrated tri-services command of the Indian Armed Forces, is hosting the first-ever Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Maritime Security Exercise in Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands. • The exercise, held from 30 October to 3 November 2026, brought together all seven BIMSTEC member countries, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand, to strengthen maritime cooperation and regional security in the Bay of Bengal. Exam Hints: ✓ What? First-ever BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise. ✓ Hosted By: India’ ANC & organized by Indian Navy. ✓ Venue: Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands. ✓ When? 30 October to 3 November 2026. ✓ Participating Countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. ✓ Theme: Banner: Shared Seas, Shared Security and Shared Prosperity, tagline – “Translating Vision to Action”. ✓ Phases: Three-day Tabletop Exercise followed by a two-day Harbour Phase. ✓ Announced At: 6th BIMSTEC Summit, held in Thailand in April 2025. Highlights of the BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise: Background: The exercise was announced by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi as a key initiative at the 6th BIMSTEC Summit, held in Thailand in April 2025 under the theme “BIMSTEC: Prosperous, Resilient and Open (PRO).”

Theme: The exercise is being conducted under the banner of “Shared Seas, Shared Security and Shared Prosperity” and the tagline “Translating Vision to Action”. Phases: The five-day exercise was organized by Indian Navy (IN) into two phases. • Tabletop: The first phase involved three days of Tabletop Exercises, focusing on scenario-based discussions, planning and coordination among participating countries. • Harbour: The second phase consists of a two-day Harbour Phase involving ships from BIMSTEC member countries, including Sri Lanka Naval Ship (SLNS) Gajabahu and Union of Myanmar Ship (UMS) King Aung Zeya, to strengthen operational coordination, mutual understanding and maritime interoperability. Significance: The Bay of Bengal is vital for regional trade, connectivity and energy security, while ANC supports maritime surveillance, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR), search and rescue, and regional engagement. About Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC); Overview: BIMSTEC promotes regional cooperation through 7 priority areas: Trade, Investment and Development; Environment and Climate Change; Security; Agriculture and Food Security; People-to-People Contact; Science, Technology and Innovation; and Connectivity. Its chairmanship rotates alphabetically among member countries, with Bangladesh assuming the chairmanship in April 2025. Establishment: BIMSTEC was established on 6 June 1997 in Bangkok, Thailand, as BIST-EC (Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand Economic Cooperation) and renamed BIMSTEC at its first Summit on 31 July 2004. Significance: BIMSTEC supports India’s Neighbourhood First and Act East policies by strengthening regional connectivity, maritime cooperation and economic development, particularly in India’s northeastern states. Secretary General – Ambassador Indra Mani Pandey (India) Headquarters: Dhaka, Bangladesh (Permanent secretariat). Assam Government Signs Rs 600 Crore MoU with Belgium’s IBA to Set Up Proton Beam Therapy Centre in Guwahati In October 2026, the Government of Assam signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Belgium-based Ion Beam Applications (IBA) to establish a Proton Beam Therapy Centre at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) in Guwahati, Assam, at an estimated cost of Rs 600 crore. • The proposed Guwahati facility will become India’s third Proton Beam Therapy Centre and the first to be established in the public health sector. Exam Hints: ✓ What? MoU signed ✓ Entities: Government of Assam and IBA Particles, Belgium ✓ Estimated Cost: Rs. 600 crore. ✓ Purpose: Establish India’s first public Proton Beam Therapy Centre at GMCH ✓ Funding: Rs. 315 crore WB loan and Rs. 285 crore from the Assam Government. ✓ Project: ASSIST ✓ Implementing Organisation: AHIDMS. About Public Proton Beam Therapy Centre: Approval: In August 2026, the Assam State Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister (CM) Himanta Biswa Sarma, approved the project under the Assam State Secondary Healthcare Initiative for Service Delivery Transformation (ASSIST). Funding: The PBT project has an estimated cost of Rs. 600 crore, jointly funded through a World Bank loan of Rs. 315 crore and a Rs. 285 crore contribution from the Government of Assam. BANKING & FINANCE SEBI Extends KYC Review Periodicity to 8 Years for Eligible Foreign Portfolio Investors In October 2026, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) released the circular “Rationalisation of periodicity of KYC review for FPIs”, extending the Know Your Customer (KYC) review periodicity for

# Page 19^page=19
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 19 Daily Content PDF eligible Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from 3 years to 8 years, to simplify regulatory compliance and improve ease of doing business. • Under the revised framework, SEBI also extended the annual KYC review period from 1 year to 2 years for specified FPIs, with the new provisions taking effect from 1 December 2026. Exam Hints: ✓ What? SEBI released circular on KYC review for FPIs ✓ Existing framework: FPI review – every one or three years ✓ Effective Date: December 1, 2026 ✓ Objective: To reduce repetitive compliance requirements and improve ease of doing business for FPIs ✓ Revised KYC Periodicity: 1 year to 2 years; 3 years to 8 years ✓ 8-Year Eligibility: Specified Category I FPIs and regulated Category II FPIs ✓ SWAGAT-FI FPIs: Existing 10-year KYC cycle retained. Existing Framework: Categories of FPI: The FPIs are broadly classified into: • Category I: This includes investors such as government-related entities, appropriately regulated funds and certain institutional investors that are considered to have a relatively lower risk profile. • Category II: This category covers a wider range of investors, including appropriately regulated entities and other eligible funds and institutions that do not qualify for Category I. Existing Framework: Under the existing framework, FPIs were required to undergo periodic KYC (Know Your Customer) reviews every one or three years, depending on their jurisdiction, category and regulatory status. Category I FPI: In the existing framework, Category I FPIs from non-high-risk jurisdictions will undergo KYC reviews once every eight years. Change Intimation Requirement: Apart from the KYC review, SEBI has removed the requirement for FPIs to intimate changes in previously submitted information or provide a declaration confirming that no changes have occurred at the time of continuing their registration. Fees Payment: The regulator has specified that FPIs must pay the continuance fee at least 15 days before the expiry of their current registration validity to facilitate a smooth continuance process. New Framework: Category I FPI: The new KYC review periodicity for Category I FPIs: • High-Risk Jurisdictions: Category I FPIs registered under Regulation 5(a)(i) will undergo KYC reviews once every eight years. • Other Category I FPIs from High-Risk Jurisdictions: KYC reviews will be conducted once every two years. • Non-High-Risk Jurisdictions: All Category I FPIs will undergo KYC reviews once every eight years. Category II FPI: The new KYC review periodicity for Category II FPIs: • High-Risk Jurisdictions: All Category II FPIs will undergo KYC reviews once every two years. • Non-High-Risk Jurisdictions – Regulated Entities: Regulated Category II FPIs will undergo KYC reviews once every eight years. • Non-High-Risk Jurisdictions – Other Entities: Other Category II FPIs will continue to undergo KYC reviews once every two years. Special Category: SEBI has retained the existing KYC review requirements for the following categories:

# Page 20^page=20
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 20 Daily Content PDF • Government Securities – FPIs (GS-FPIs): The review periodicity for these securities will remain linked to the KYC review requirements to their respective bank accounts under the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines. • SWAGAT-FI (Single Window Automatic and Generalised Access for Trusted Foreign Investors) FPIs: The existing 10 year KYC review cycle will continue. Fee Payment: Under the revised provisions, FPIs seeking to continue their registration for another three- year period, or 10 years in the case of SWAGAT-FI, will be required to pay the applicable fees to their Designated Depository Participants (DDPs). Note: Regulation 5(a)(i) of the SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations, 2019 deals with Government and Government-related investors that are eligible for registration as Category I Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs). About Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI): The SEBI, a market regulator, was constituted as a non-statutory body on April 12,1988 through a resolution of the Government of India (GoI) and was established as a statutory body in 1992.
